agree.reason: Mark likes Daniela and would see a tidy record, but he thinks the renovation drove the scores. The memo only says the check-in score measures the desk. It never shows that the score had already reached 8.2 before the renovation began, so his main doubt stands.

honest.reason: The memo drops the unsupported 'main reason' claim and admits the renovation helped. Its figures match the brief. The only stretch is 'more experienced than before', which is a reasonable inference from lower turnover rather than a stated fact.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the turnover counts into 64% and 36% and calls the cut from 9 shifts to 5 'almost half'. It leaves out three of the strongest true figures: the 7.9-to-8.2 rise before the renovation, no uncovered shifts in the 7 weeks, and overtime under plan.

right_comparison.reason: The real alternative is the outside candidate, and the memo never mentions or weighs them. It also never splits the score trend into before and after the renovation.

qualification.reason: The budget plan has a 90-day window and a monthly labor-cost report. But the finance course is only a bracketed placeholder, the controller sessions aren't named, and nothing sets a checkable number or says what happens if a target is missed.

objections.reason: The budget gap is faced openly and the renovation gets a weak partial answer. The outside candidate's experience at a larger hotel, which is the GM's other main reason to hesitate, is never addressed.

fit.reason: It is a one-page memo as asked. But it is full of unfilled brackets for names, the review site, duties and the course, even though the names were available, so it can't be sent as it is.
